description: An emulation of a microcassette recorder: it writes whatever arrives at the audio input onto a tape kept inside the patch, and plays it back forwards or backwards at any speed

params.text: Halts the tape while a play button stays on, so the reels can be turned by hand
Winds the tape forward at the multiple of play speed set by the Fast Speed screw; Ctrl and a click jumps to the next loop point instead, and Ctrl with Shift jumps to the end of the tape
Winds the tape backwards at the multiple of play speed set by the Fast Speed screw; Ctrl and a click jumps to the previous loop point instead, and Ctrl with Shift jumps to the start
Sets how fast the two winding buttons move the tape, from a quarter of play speed to 20 times it
Nothing in the module reads this screw. It sets the rise rate of a slew limiter on the tape speed whose every use is commented out of the source, so turning it changes no sound.
Sets the tempo the tape is measured in, 1 to 360 BPM; the tempo output pulses at it and the loop points are counted in its bars
Sets how many beats make a bar, 1 to 48, which fixes how much tape one bar covers
Sets the bar the loop starts at, 0 to 99
Sets the bar the loop ends at, 0 to 99

Turn a reel to move the tape by hand, which scratches the recording while a play button and pause are both on. Dragging near the rim brakes the tape and dragging at the centre leaves it at full speed.
Sets the loop start to the bar the tape has reached, and springs back off
Sets the loop end to the bar the tape has reached, and springs back off

inputs.text: The audio written to the tape, one polyphonic channel per track. It is also the bus back from the Tape Recorder Mixer, whose channels 5 to 8 erase a track and whose channels 9 to 12 saturate it.
Moves the loop start, one bar per 1/12V, added to the loop start knob and never taken below bar 0
Moves the loop end, one bar per 1/12V, added to the loop end knob and never taken below bar 0
Multiplies the tape speed by two to the power of the voltage, so 1V plays the tape an octave higher and -1V an octave lower
A rising edge toggles the pause button

outputs.text: The tape playback, one polyphonic channel per track, at ten times the value stored on the tape; while the tape is not running this carries the audio input instead
The speed the tape is running at as a pitch, one volt per octave; the sign is dropped, so a reversed tape reads at the speed a forward one would
5V for each beat and 10V for the first beat of a bar, one millisecond long, as the tape passes them; nothing comes out unless a play button is on
5V while the tape plays forward, -5V while it plays backwards, 0V when it is stopped

notes: recording is always on. Whenever a play button is on, whatever is at the audio input is written to the tape as it passes; to play a tape back without spoiling it, unpatch the audio input.
the loop is off while the loop start and loop end read the same bar.
the two winding buttons are momentary while a play button is on, and latch when the tape is stopped.
the Ctrl in the winding shortcuts is Cmd on a Mac, and holding Ctrl or Ctrl and Shift while turning a reel moves the tape more slowly.
the tape is kept inside the patch. Saving the patch writes the recording beside it as tape.wav, and saving a module preset writes a .wav of the same name beside the preset.
menu: the text field at the top — holds the name written on the cassette label
Cassette Label: 1970, Red, Green, Purple, Brown, Rainbow, Stars, Snowflake, Flowers, Tape, Chip, Zzz — chooses the artwork printed on the cassette
Tape Length — sets how long the tape is, from MC 1 for one minute to MC 120 for two hours, and returns the transport to the start; MC 120 is barred while the track count is 4 Tracks
Track Count: Mono, Stereo, 4 Tracks — sets how many tracks the tape carries and how many channels the audio output has; 4 Tracks is barred on an MC 120 tape
Loop Mode: Cycle, Ping-Pong — chooses what happens at a loop point, Cycle jumping to the other end and Ping-Pong reversing the play direction; a new module comes up on Ping-Pong
Erase Tape — writes silence over the whole tape
